subject.title: Import Scrollmark and twitter-web-exporter captures into the canonical local store

question: Should Birdclaw adopt Scrollmark canonical bundle v1 as a supported core ingestion contract, and what provenance and collection-completeness fields must become durable and backup-covered?
rationale: The file-import boundary fits the vision, but choosing an external schema and permanent merge semantics affects Birdclaw’s storage contract and cannot be safely inferred by an implementation worker.

options.title: Adopt Scrollmark v1 first
options.body: Support only the versioned canonical bundle initially, with explicit producer, schema, observation, import-run, and partial-completeness metadata.

options.title: Design a neutral envelope first
options.body: Define a Birdclaw-owned producer-neutral capture schema before implementing adapters for either external tool.

options.title: Defer third-party imports
options.body: Keep official archives and Birdclaw-owned live transports as the only supported ingestion sources for now.

recommendation.title: Adopt Scrollmark v1 first
recommendation.body: Support only the versioned canonical bundle initially, with explicit producer, schema, observation, import-run, and partial-completeness metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available owner for the durable product and storage-boundary choice based on recent canonical-store and vision work.
